records.headline: Make the follow-up do the remembering.
records.body: When your idea comes back wearing someone else's name, use the record—not a public accusation. In an approved AI tool, use only facts you may share and ask for a neutral recap: what you proposed, when, what was decided and who owns the next step. Check every line before sending.

records.headline: Give one repeat task a dress rehearsal—not the keys.
records.body: A reusable AI skill can save instructions, scripts and reference files so the same process is available when a matching job comes up. Start with one low-risk task you already know how to judge, such as turning fictional meeting notes into a draft action list. Outside work, run the same rehearsal with an imaginary trip before a packing skill sees real bookings. Read every bundled file, check what it can access, and test a normal case, an awkward case and a case where it should not run. If you cannot spot a bad result or stop the workflow, it is not ready for real work.
records.audienceJob: Give a non-technical reader one bounded, current first-use test for a reusable AI skill without endorsing third-party packs or implying that a procedure replaces accountable staff.

records.headline: Mercury is in regression.
records.body: Today’s forecast: change one thing, then check the receipts. Save a few representative examples of a repeated task—say, summarising fictional meeting notes at work and planning meals from an invented cupboard at home—and write down what a good answer must include. Change one instruction at a time, then rerun the same examples. If the new prompt sounds smoother but fails a case the old one passed, that is a regression, not growth. Mercury is innocent.
records.audienceJob: Use the horoscope form to teach one repeatable prompt-evaluation habit: compare bounded revisions against the same representative examples and acceptance criteria.

records.headline: Put the name back on the idea.
records.body: You make a useful point, the meeting moves on, and ten minutes later the same point gets applause in somebody else’s voice. You do not need to prosecute motive in real time. Reconnect the idea and keep the work moving: ‘Yes—that builds on the customer-risk point I raised earlier. The next decision is…’ If you are the colleague who noticed, try: ‘Building on Maya’s point about customer risk…’ Afterward, send a three-line recap: the contribution, the decision and the next owner. That record preserves context; it does not prove why the idea was repeated. The AI mirror is narrow but useful: a polished AI answer can also repeat a claim after its source has disappeared. Keep the original link or document attached and verify it before relying on the retelling. At home, do the same before forwarding a glossy health claim in the family chat. People are not citation objects, and a version history cannot diagnose intent. If this is a repeated pattern, a power problem or a material career consequence, take the facts to a manager, sponsor or appropriate workplace channel—the meeting line is a first move, not the whole fix.
records.audienceJob: Give a professional reader exact low-drama language for restoring contribution context, a neutral recap structure and a truthful AI-source mirror without reducing a structural workplace problem to confidence or prompting.
